findings.claim: New behavior: once the port says a result is classified, the session records the classified- key, and classifyRuling never asks the port about that result again in the session (classify.go:129-135). Before this change the port was asked at every stop. If the page later stops holding the result's Evidence row in the same session (the agent reverts or edits docs/wiki, or a consolidation deletes the row, a case L67 names for T6), the result has a kept finding the page lacks, but the stop hook stays silent until a new session starts. No test pins or documents this case: the Stop doc (stop.go:52-54) says only that the result is not asked of the port again. Failure mode: port returns true at stop 1, the row is removed, and stop 2 does not block although the page now lacks the result.

keptResultsOf now returns on the first stored result it cannot read, hold or bind, in any feature of the tree and any branch commit. So one corrupt or unreadable file, for example a verdict that cannot be read, suppresses the classification question for every other result of the branch at every stop until it is fixed, and the only signal is a stderr line that shows in verbose mode only. This is the tradeoff L67 accepted under choice 1 and lists under Risks. The code, its doc comment and J1/J3 match the design. The cost is reported because it is a new failure mode on the stop hook's path: collecting the per-result errors and still asking for the results that do hold would keep both the signal and the other questions.
